How to verify. Set the weights you care about, note the top parcels, then open a few in Google Maps and judge whether they are genuinely open, developable ground. Then flip the vacancy source to v1 and repeat. The v1 model is the original spectral-threshold one whose reported 98.5% accuracy was circular — it correlates just −0.085 with built-up density, where v8 reaches −0.651. A vacancy score must fall as built-up density rises, so that gap is the clearest single indicator of which model is measuring something real.

Caveats. The five OSM subscores are unchanged and were never audited in this work — education and essential-services in particular average near 2/100, meaning almost every parcel scores zero and those sliders do very little. Parcels marked verified are the 254 checked against 0.57 m/px imagery; the rest are model predictions. The v8 model is validated as a ranking over this AOI in the Jan–Mar dry season, not as an area estimate and not across seasons.
